title: Generating AI Literacy MCQs: A Multi-Agent LLM Approach
venue: Proceedings of the 56th ACM Technical Symposium on Computer Science Education V. 2 (SIGCSE TS 2025)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the lack of scalable, reliable assessment materials for AI literacy in K-12 education. The authors ask whether a multi-agent large language model (LLM) workflow can generate high-quality multiple-choice questions (MCQs) aligned to learning objectives, grade level, and Bloom’s taxonomy for AI literacy instruction.

The proposed intervention is a generator-and-critic workflow built with LangGraph and OpenAI’s gpt-4o-mini model. A generator agent creates MCQs from user inputs, and two critique agents review them for language/grade-level appropriateness and item-writing flaws. A supervisor agent either approves items or sends them back for revision. The system produced 40 MCQs for grades K7-9, and three K-12 AI literacy experts evaluated the items using a rubric covering correctness, clarity, relevance, Bloom’s level, grade-level fit, and classroom usability.

The evaluation found generally strong expert agreement that the questions were understandable, answerable, grammatical, clearly worded, and closely related to the learning objectives. Experts also largely judged the items to be usable in class, though there was some disagreement on whether certain items needed rephrasing, matched the intended Bloom’s level, or were appropriate for the target grade level. Overall, the paper concludes that the multi-agent approach shows promise for producing pedagogically sound AI literacy assessment items, but it remains an early-stage system requiring classroom testing and further validation.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic large language model-based AI system used to automatically generate and critique multiple-choice questions for educational assessment.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in a multi-agent workflow to generate and refine AI literacy multiple-choice questions for grades K-9, with critique agents checking readability, grade-level alignment, and item-writing flaws.

findings.finding_summary: This paper is not an empirical classroom or learning-outcome study. In a preliminary expert review of 40 LLM-generated AI literacy MCQs, three experts judged the items to be generally well formed and aligned with learning objectives, with high agreement on correctness (97.5%, 85%, and 85%) and strong ratings for understandability, answerability, grammaticality, clarity, and relevance. However, the study reports disagreement on rephrasing, Bloom's level, and grade-level appropriateness, and notes that classroom effectiveness has not yet been tested.
findings.measure: Expert rubric ratings of generated multiple-choice questions

quality_tier_rationale: This is a framework/prototype paper with expert evaluation only, not a randomized, quasi-experimental, or classroom-based study of reading or literacy outcomes. It does not provide direct comparative evidence against instruction or other tools.
impact_tier_rationale: No student outcome effect size is reported, so instructional impact cannot be estimated. The paper suggests potential utility for assessment generation, but the evidence is limited to expert judgments rather than measured learning effects.
